mainTopic: Which wives drink the סוטה water, and why the משנה and ברייתא needed to spell out each case
overview: This amud sorts out which wives go through the סוטה process. It starts with the end of a ברייתא. If the marriage itself was forbidden, the woman neither drinks nor collects her כתובה. If the marriage was allowed, she drinks, or loses her כתובה if she refuses. Because that ברייתא lists an איילונית among the women who drink, the גמרא challenges רב נחמן. He answers that this is a dispute among תנאים and that he follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, who learns from 'וְנִקְּתָה וְנִזְרְעָה זָרַע' that only a woman able to have children drinks. The other side reads that פסוק as a blessing for the innocent woman. רבי עקיבא and רבי ישמעאל argue over what that blessing is. The גמרא then asks 'isn't it obvious?' about several cases: the wife of a ממזר, the wife of a גר, the wife of a כהן and her being permitted to her husband, and the wife of a סריס. For each one it shows the mistaken idea the teaching comes to rule out. The amud ends by asking why the משנה needs to say a warning works for all עריות, and the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Pregnant or nursing from another man: no drinking, no כתובה
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר rules that a woman who married while pregnant or nursing from another man neither drinks nor collects her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman pregnant from another man, or nursing another man's baby, does not drink the bitter water and does not get her כתובה. This is the view of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues its list of women who do not drink the סוטה water. It adds a woman whose husband married her while she was pregnant or nursing from someone else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule follows the ברייתא's pattern: if the marriage should not have happened, there is no סוטה process and no כתובה. The next line explains why רבי מאיר sees this marriage as forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: A pregnant woman
A nursing woman
Of his fellow, meaning another man's child
They drink (the bitter water of a סוטה)
The marriage contract payment owed to a wife

phrases.english: A woman pregnant with another man's child
and a woman nursing another man's child
neither drink nor collect their marriage contract
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא's list of women who neither drink nor collect a כתובה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman who married while pregnant or nursing from another man neither drinks nor collects her כתובה, according to רבי מאיר.

steps.title: רבי מאיר's reason: this marriage is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר holds that a man may not marry such a woman, and if he does, he must divorce her and may never take her back.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר used to say: a man should not marry a woman pregnant from another man or nursing another man's child. If he did marry her, he must divorce her and may never remarry her.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains why רבי מאיר said she does not drink: in his view the marriage itself is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the marriage is forbidden, she falls into the group of women who neither drink nor collect a כתובה. רבי מאיר is strict: the divorce is permanent, and the husband can never take her back.

keyTerms.meaning: He should not marry
He must send her out, meaning divorce her
He may never take her back

phrases.english: For Rabbi Meir used to say:
A person may not marry a woman pregnant from another man
or one nursing another man's child,
and if he married her, he must divorce her
and may never take her back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind רבי מאיר's ruling in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Marrying a woman who is pregnant or nursing from another man is forbidden. If it happens, he must divorce her permanently.

steps.title: חכמים: divorce now, remarry later
steps.stepSummary: חכמים agree he must divorce her, but he may marry her again once the waiting time is over.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים say: he must divorce her, and when the time comes when he would have been allowed to marry her, he may marry her.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים argue with רבי מאיר about the penalty. They agree he must divorce her, but they say the divorce does not have to be permanent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree the marriage was not allowed at that time. The disagreement is only whether he may ever take her back. The חכמים say he may, once the waiting period for the baby has passed.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the majority opinion
His time, meaning when he would be allowed to marry her
To bring her in as a wife

phrases.english: And the Sages say: he must divorce her,
and when his time to marry her arrives, he may marry her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי מאיר about whether the divorce is permanent.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: He divorces her but may remarry her once the waiting period is over.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר and חכמים both forbid marrying a woman pregnant or nursing from another man. They argue only about whether the husband can ever take her back.

steps.title: Young man who married a barren or elderly woman
steps.stepSummary: A young man with no wife or children who marries a woman who cannot have children: she neither drinks nor collects her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A young man who married a barren or elderly woman, and he never had a wife and children before, she does not drink and does not get her כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds another forbidden marriage: a young man who has no children yet marries a woman who cannot have children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He has not yet fulfilled פריה ורביה, so a marriage that cannot produce children counts as forbidden. That puts her in the group that neither drinks nor collects a כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: A young man
A barren woman
An elderly woman
From before

phrases.english: And a young man who married a barren or elderly woman,
and he does not already have a wife and children from before,
she neither drinks nor collects her marriage contract.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new case of a forbidden marriage to the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A childless young man who marries a woman who cannot bear children is in a forbidden marriage, so she neither drinks nor collects.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: he can have children through another wife
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says this marriage is not forbidden, since he can marry another woman and have children with her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: he can marry another woman and have children through her.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר disagrees with the previous ruling about the young man's marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In his view, marrying a barren woman does not stop the man from having children, because he can take another wife. So the marriage is allowed, and she is treated like any regular wife for the סוטה rules.

keyTerms.meaning: Another woman
To be fruitful and multiply, meaning to have children
From her

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says:
He is able to marry another woman
and be fruitful and multiply through her.
phrases.notes: "Her" means the other wife, not the barren one.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: יָכוֹל הוּא לִישָּׂא אַחֶרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with step 4 by arguing that the marriage is not forbidden.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The marriage is allowed because he can have children through another wife.

steps.title: Warned while betrothed, secluded after marriage
steps.stepSummary: If he warned his ארוסה or שומרת יבם, and she secluded herself after he married her, she either drinks or loses her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if a man warned his betrothed, or the woman waiting for him as her יבם, and she was secluded with the other man after he married her, then she either drinks or does not get her כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now switches to the other group: cases where she does go through the סוטה process. The first case is a warning given before marriage, with seclusion that happened after marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אבל marks the contrast with the forbidden cases. Since the seclusion happened after a proper marriage, she is a full wife, so she must drink. If she refuses, she loses her כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: One who warns his wife not to be alone with a certain man
His betrothed (after קידושין, before נישואין)
A widow waiting for her late husband's brother to marry her
She secluded herself with the other man

steps.confusionAlert: "Either drinks or does not collect" does not mean the husband picks one. It means she must drink, and if she refuses to drink, she loses her כתובה.

phrases.english: But one who warns his betrothed
or the widow waiting for him as her יבם,
and after he married her she secluded herself,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שׁוֹתָה, אוֹ לֹא נוֹטֶלֶת כְּתוּבָּה.
phrases.english: she either drinks or does not collect her marriage contract.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the forbidden-marriage cases to cases where she does drink.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A warning given before marriage still counts if the seclusion happened after the marriage. She must drink or lose her כתובה.

steps.title: His own pregnant or nursing wife
steps.stepSummary: A wife who is pregnant or nursing his own child still goes through the סוטה process: she drinks or loses her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she is pregnant with or nursing his own child, she either drinks or does not get her כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא contrasts step 1. When the pregnancy or nursing is from the husband himself, the marriage is perfectly allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What made the earlier case a problem was a marriage to a woman carrying or nursing another man's child. Here nothing was wrong with the marriage, so the regular rule applies: she drinks, or she loses her כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: His own

phrases.english: A woman pregnant with or nursing his own child

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שׁוֹתָה, אוֹ לֹא נוֹטֶלֶת כְּתוּבָּתָהּ.
phrases.english: either drinks or does not collect her marriage contract.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors step 1, but with the husband's own child.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: His own pregnant or nursing wife drinks, or else loses her כתובה.

steps.title: Young man who already has a wife and children
steps.stepSummary: If the young man already has a wife and children, marrying a barren or elderly woman is allowed, so she drinks or loses her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A young man who married a barren or elderly woman, and he already has a wife and children, she either drinks or does not get her כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא contrasts step 4. Since this man already has children, nothing is wrong with the marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only problem in step 4 was that he had not yet had children. Once that is no longer an issue, she is a regular wife and goes through the regular סוטה rule.

keyTerms.meaning: And he has
Children

steps.whatToRemember: The key question in this ברייתא is whether the marriage was allowed. A forbidden marriage means no drinking and no כתובה. An allowed marriage means she drinks, or loses her כתובה if she refuses.

phrases.english: A young man who married a barren or elderly woman,
and he has a wife and children,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שׁוֹתָה, אוֹ לֹא נוֹטֶלֶת כְּתוּבָּה.
phrases.english: she either drinks or does not collect her marriage contract.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָרוֹבֶא שֶׁנָּשָׂא עֲקָרָה וּזְקֵינָה, וְיֵשׁ לוֹ אִשָּׁה וּבָנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors step 4, but with a man who already has children.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: When the marriage is allowed, the wife either drinks or forfeits her כתובה.

steps.title: The end of the ברייתא: permitted marriages, including an איילונית
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes its list. The wives of a ממזר, a נתין, a גר or a freed slave, and also an איילונית, all drink or lose their כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ממזר's wife who is also a ממזרת, a נתין's wife who is also a נתינה, the wife of a גר or a freed slave, and an איילונית: each one either drinks or does not collect her כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its list of women whose marriages are allowed, so the סוטה process applies to them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are all marriages that are permitted, so the woman drinks or loses her כתובה. The key new item is איילונית. She is in the same list, which means a woman who cannot bear children can still drink.

keyTerms.meaning: A child born from a forbidden union, who may marry another ממזר
A descendant of the גבעונים, who may marry another נתין
A freed slave
A woman who never developed physically and cannot bear children

phrases.english: The wife of a mamzer who is married to a mamzer,
phrases.notes: He means a ממזרת married to a ממזר. That marriage is allowed.

phrases.english: and the wife of a Gibeonite married to a Gibeonite,
and the wife of a convert or of a freed slave,
and a woman who cannot bear children,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שׁוֹתָה, אוֹ לֹא נוֹטֶלֶת כְּתוּבָּה.
phrases.english: either drinks or does not collect her marriage contract.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun in the earlier steps.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In permitted marriages, including that of an איילונית, the wife drinks or loses her כתובה.

steps.title: The ברייתא includes an איילונית, so it refutes רב נחמן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the ברייתא says an איילונית drinks. That contradicts רב נחמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, the ברייתא teaches that an איילונית drinks. This is a refutation of רב נחמן!
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא explains why it quoted the whole ברייתא. The line about איילונית contradicts רב נחמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן held that an איילונית does not go through the סוטה process. The ברייתא clearly says she does, so his view seems to be refuted.

keyTerms.meaning: In any case, it teaches. This points to the one line that matters.
A strong refutation

phrases.english: In any event, it teaches that a woman who cannot bear children drinks,
this is a refutation of Rav Naḥman!

steps.triggerLanguage: קָתָנֵי מִיהָא אַיְילוֹנִית, תְּיוּבְתֵּיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא from Step 9 to attack רב נחמן.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling that an איילונית does not drink
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא explicitly says an איילונית drinks or loses her כתובה.

steps.title: רב נחמן: this is a dispute among תנאים, and I follow רבי שמעון בן אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says the question is a dispute among תנאים. He follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, who learns from the פסוק that only a woman able to bear children drinks.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן would answer: This is a dispute among תנאים, and I follow this תנא. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says an איילונית neither drinks nor collects her כתובה, because the פסוק says "she shall be cleared and shall conceive seed." That means a woman who normally can bear children, which leaves out this woman.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן defends himself. He does not have to agree with that ברייתא, because another תנא holds just like him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא represents one side of a dispute among תנאים, so it cannot refute רב נחמן. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר reads "וְנִקְּתָה וְנִזְרְעָה זָרַע" as saying the סוטה process is only for a woman able to have children. An איילונית is left out.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute among תנאים
"She shall be cleared and shall conceive seed" (במדבר 5:28)
To conceive and bear children

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman could have said to you:
It is a dispute between tanna'im,
and I hold like this tanna,

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: as it is taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:

phrases.aramaic: אַיְילוֹנִית — לֹא שׁוֹתָה וְלֹא נוֹטֶלֶת כְּתוּבָּה,
phrases.english: A woman who cannot bear children neither drinks nor collects her marriage contract,
as it is stated: "And she shall be cleared, and shall conceive seed,"
meaning one whose way is to bear children,
which excludes this woman, whose way is not to bear children.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְךָ רַב נַחְמָן: תַּנָּאֵי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the refutation in Step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Dispute among תנאים: רב נחמן sides with a different תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is the only view, so רב נחמן is refuted.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר holds like רב נחמן, based on "וְנִקְּתָה וְנִזְרְעָה זָרַע".
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common way the גמרא saves an אמורא: he may follow one side of a dispute among תנאים.

steps.title: What do the רבנן learn from "וְנִקְּתָה וְנִזְרְעָה זָרַע"?
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן hold that an איילונית drinks. So the גמרא asks what they do with the פסוק that רבי שמעון בן אלעזר used.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן, what do they do with this פסוק, "she shall be cleared and shall conceive seed"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next move. It asks how the other side reads the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every פסוק must teach something. If the רבנן don't use it to leave out an איילונית, they must learn something else from it.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the majority view (here, the ברייתא that lets an איילונית drink)
What do they do with it? (What do they learn from this פסוק?)

phrases.english: And the Rabbis,
phrases.notes: These are the תנאים of the ברייתא who said an איילונית does drink.

phrases.english: this verse, "And she shall be cleared, and shall conceive seed,"
what do they do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן, הַאי ״וְנִקְּתָה וְנִזְרְעָה זָרַע״ מַאי עָבְדִי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on the פסוק used in Step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the רבנן learn from "וְנִקְּתָה וְנִזְרְעָה זָרַע"

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: a barren woman who is found innocent will have children
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן need the פסוק for another teaching. רבי עקיבא says that if the סוטה was barren and the water clears her, she will have children.
steps.simpleTranslation: They need it for what was taught in a ברייתא: "She shall be cleared and shall conceive seed" teaches that if she was barren, she will be blessed with children. These are the words of רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the רבנן use the פסוק for a promise of blessing to the innocent woman. They do not use it to leave anyone out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי עקיבא, the פסוק describes a reward. A barren woman who is proven innocent will now conceive. Since the פסוק teaches this, it does not have to exclude an איילונית.

keyTerms.meaning: They need it for something else
A barren woman
She is remembered (blessed with a child)

phrases.english: They need it for that which is taught:
"And she shall be cleared, and shall conceive [seed],"
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording, to match the פסוק.

phrases.english: teaching that if she was barren, she will be remembered and conceive,
this is the statement of Rabbi Akiva.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק teaches that an innocent barren סוטה will conceive (רבי עקיבא).

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל objects: barren women would seclude themselves on purpose
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל argues that רבי עקיבא's reading leads to a strange result. Barren women would seclude themselves to win the blessing, and a good woman would lose out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל said to him: If so, all barren women will seclude themselves and be blessed with children, and this one, because she did not seclude herself, loses out?!
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the same ברייתא, רבי ישמעאל challenges רבי עקיבא's reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If being cleared cures barrenness, a barren woman would gain by going into seclusion on purpose and drinking. The woman who behaves properly would miss the blessing. That makes no sense, so רבי ישמעאל rejects this reading.

keyTerms.meaning: They will seclude themselves (be alone with a man)
Since, because
She loses out

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael said to him:

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן, יִסָּתְרוּ כׇּל הָעֲקָרוֹת וְיִפָּקְדוּ,
phrases.english: If so, all the barren women will seclude themselves and be remembered,
and this one, since she did not seclude herself, loses out?!
phrases.notes: "This one" is the proper barren woman who stayed away from seclusion.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל: אִם כֵּן, יִסָּתְרוּ כׇּל הָעֲקָרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי עקיבא's reading from Step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's reading that an innocent barren סוטה will conceive
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It would reward forbidden seclusion and leave the proper woman without the blessing.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל's reading: the innocent woman's births improve
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל explains the פסוק differently. A woman who already has children will now give birth more easily and to better children.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what does the פסוק "she shall be cleared and shall conceive seed" teach? That if she used to give birth in pain, she will give birth with ease. If she had girls, she will have boys. If short children, tall ones. If dark children, fair ones.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל gives his own explanation of the פסוק. The blessing is an improvement in her births, not a cure for barrenness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי ישמעאל's reading, the פסוק promises better births to a woman who can already have children. So no barren woman has a reason to seclude herself on purpose. Either way, the רבנן use the פסוק for a blessing and not to exclude an איילונית.

keyTerms.meaning: What does the פסוק come to teach?
In pain
With ease

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: an איילונית does not drink, because the פסוק is about a woman who can bear children. The רבנן disagree. They read the same פסוק as a blessing for the innocent woman, either a barren woman conceiving (רבי עקיבא) or easier and better births (רבי ישמעאל).

phrases.english: If so, what does the verse teach when it says:
"And she shall be cleared, and shall conceive seed"?

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאִם הָיְתָה יוֹלֶדֶת בְּצַעַר — יוֹלֶדֶת בְּרֶיוַח,
phrases.english: That if she used to give birth in pain, she will give birth with ease;
if she gave birth to females, she will give birth to males;
if to short children, she will give birth to tall ones;
if to dark children, she will give birth to fair ones.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״וְנִקְּתָה וְנִזְרְעָה זָרַע״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי ישמעאל replaces the reading he rejected in Step 14 with his own.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק promises an innocent סוטה easier and better births, not a cure for barrenness.

steps.title: Why say the wife of a ממזר drinks?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא that the wife of a ממזר married to a ממזר drinks, and asks why this needs to be said.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא says: the wife of a ממזר who is married to a ממזר drinks. Isn't that obvious?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the list in the ברייתא and quotes the case of a ממזר married to a ממזרת. It asks why the ברייתא bothered to say something that seems obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ממזר is allowed to marry a ממזרת, so this is a normal, permitted marriage. Since the סוטה process applies to any permitted marriage, there seems to be nothing new here.

keyTerms.meaning: A child born from a forbidden relationship. He may marry only someone of the same status.
'It is obvious!' The גמרא's way of asking why a statement needed to be said.

phrases.english: The wife of a mamzer, married to a mamzer.
That is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the איילונית discussion to the next case in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's need to say that the wife of a ממזר drinks.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Their marriage is permitted, so of course the סוטה rules apply. Saying it seems unnecessary.

steps.title: We might have avoided creating more ממזרים
steps.stepSummary: Without the ברייתא, we might think she should not drink, so that the couple would not stay together and have more ממזר children.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: we should not increase the number of people with flawed lineage. So the ברייתא teaches us that she does drink.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the ברייתא needed to say this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she drinks and is found innocent, she goes back to her husband, and their children will also be ממזרים. One might think we should avoid that result and not let her drink. The ברייתא teaches that this worry does not stop the סוטה process.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What might you have said?' This introduces the mistaken idea the teaching comes to reject.
Increasing the number of people with flawed lineage.
'It teaches us.' This shows what the source came to teach.

phrases.english: What might you have said?
We should not increase the number of people of flawed lineage.
So it teaches us that she does drink.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא question of step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: shows there was a real reason to think otherwise
steps.terutzHavaAmina: She should not drink, so that more ממזרים are not born.
steps.terutzMaskana: She drinks. Worry about more ממזרים does not cancel the סוטה process.

steps.title: Why say the wife of a גר drinks?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next case in the ברייתא: the wife of a גר or a freed slave, and an איילונית. It asks why the case of the גר needs to be said.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא says: the wife of a גר, the wife of a freed slave, and an איילונית all drink. Isn't that obvious?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next part of the ברייתא and asks again, 'isn't this obvious?'
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גר or a freed slave is fully Jewish and has a valid marriage. So it seems obvious that his wife would go through the סוטה process like anyone else.

keyTerms.meaning: A convert to Judaism.
A freed slave. He has the status of a convert.

steps.confusionAlert: The question and answer here are only about the גר and the freed slave. The איילונית was already discussed in the earlier steps.

phrases.english: The wife of a convert or of a freed slave
and a woman who cannot have children (drink).
Isn't that obvious?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next case in the same ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's need to say that the wife of a גר drinks.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A גר's marriage is fully valid, so the סוטה rules should obviously apply.

steps.title: The פסוק says 'בני ישראל'
steps.stepSummary: One might have thought the פסוק limits סוטה to people born Jewish, because it says 'בני ישראל'.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: the פסוק says 'Speak to the children of Israel,' and not to converts. So the ברייתא teaches us that she does drink.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the ברייתא needed to mention the גר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'בני ישראל' could be read as 'only those born of Israel,' which would leave out גרים. The ברייתא teaches that גרים are included.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The children of Israel.' Read narrowly, it could mean only those born Jewish.

phrases.english: What might you have said?
"Speak to the children of Israel,"
and not to converts.
So it teaches us that she does drink.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא question of step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא based on how the פסוק might be read
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'בני ישראל' leaves out גרים, so the wife of a גר would not drink.
steps.terutzMaskana: The wife of a גר does drink.

steps.title: Maybe גרים really are left out
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: why not accept that הוה אמינא? Maybe the פסוק really does leave out גרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But why not say that this is indeed so?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back. The reading that left out גרים sounds good, so why reject it? This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the wife of a גר drinks, but the פסוק seems to say only 'בני ישראל.' The גמרא wants a source in the פסוק that includes גרים.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Say that it is indeed so.' This challenges the rejected idea by suggesting it might be correct.

phrases.english: But say that it is indeed so!
phrases.notes: He means: maybe גרים really are left out by the words 'בני ישראל.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rejection of the הוה אמינא in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that the wife of a גר drinks.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק's wording 'בני ישראל' seems to support leaving out גרים.

steps.title: 'וְאָמַרְתָּ' includes גרים
steps.stepSummary: The extra word 'וְאָמַרְתָּ' in the פסוק is a ריבוי that adds גרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And say" is an inclusion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that another word in the same פסוק includes גרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could have stopped at 'Speak to the children of Israel.' The added words 'and say to them' widen the group to include גרים. So the narrow reading is overruled.

keyTerms.meaning: An inclusion: a word in the פסוק that adds more cases.
'And you shall say.' The word in במדבר 5:12 that includes גרים.

steps.whatToRemember: The wife of a ממזר and the wife of a גר both drink. Worry about more ממזרים does not stop it, and 'וְאָמַרְתָּ' includes גרים.

phrases.english: "And say" is an inclusion.
phrases.notes: These are the next words in the same פסוק, במדבר 5:12. They add גרים to the group.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a word in the פסוק that includes more cases
steps.terutzMaskana: 'וְאָמַרְתָּ' includes גרים, so the wife of a גר drinks.

steps.title: Why say the wife of a כהן drinks?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that the wife of a כהן drinks, and asks why this needs to be said.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: the wife of a כהן drinks. Why say that the wife of a כהן drinks? It is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns back to our משנה and asks why it needed to say the case of a כהן's wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She is married to her husband in a fully valid marriage. So it seems obvious she would go through the סוטה process.

keyTerms.meaning: The wife of a כהן.
She drinks the bitter water.

phrases.english: The wife of a priest drinks, etc.
The wife of a priest drinks?
That is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the ברייתא and returns to a line in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement that the wife of a כהן drinks.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Her marriage is permitted, so of course the סוטה rules apply.

steps.title: Forbidden even if forced, so maybe she does not drink
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק suggests the סוטה process is for a woman who would be permitted if she had been forced. A כהן's wife is forbidden even then, so one might think she does not drink. The משנה teaches that she does.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: the פסוק says 'and she was not forced,' which means that if she was not forced she is forbidden, but if she was forced she is permitted. And this woman, since she is forbidden even if she was forced, you might say she does not drink. So the משנה teaches us that she does.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the משנה needed to teach that a כהן's wife drinks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'וְהִיא לֹא נִתְפָּשָׂה' shows that an ordinary woman who was forced stays permitted to her husband. That suggests the water is only for a woman whose status depends on whether she acted willingly. A כהן's wife is forbidden to him even if she was forced, so one might think the water does nothing for her, but the משנה says she still drinks.

keyTerms.meaning: She was seized, meaning taken by force (raped).
Since.

steps.whatToRemember: The wife of a כהן drinks, even though she would be forbidden to him even if she had been forced.

phrases.english: What might you have said?
"And she was not seized": then she is forbidden.
But if she was seized, she is permitted.
And this one, since even if seized she is forbidden,
you might say she should not drink.
So it teaches us that she does drink.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא question of step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא based on reading the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The סוטה process is only for a woman who would be permitted if she had been forced. A כהן's wife is not like that, so she would not drink.
steps.terutzMaskana: The wife of a כהן drinks anyway.

steps.title: Isn't it obvious she is permitted to her husband?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling that the כהן's wife is permitted to her husband after drinking, and asks why this needs saying.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says she is permitted to her husband. Isn't that obvious?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next words of the משנה about the כהן's wife and asks why they are needed. If the water showed she is innocent, of course she may stay with her husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 23 explained why the כהן's wife drinks at all. Now the גמרא looks at the next phrase. An innocent woman returning to her husband seems too obvious to need stating.

keyTerms.meaning: And she is permitted to her husband
It is obvious! (the גמרא asking why something needs saying)

phrases.english: And she is permitted to her husband.
It is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause about the same כהן's wife.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the water cleared her, being permitted to her husband follows automatically, so the clause looks unnecessary.

steps.title: רב הונא: The case is a woman who weakens
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא explains that the משנה is speaking about a woman whose body weakened after drinking.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: It is talking about a woman who becomes weak.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers that the משנה is not talking about a simple case. It means a woman who grew weak or ill after drinking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she became sick, we might suspect she is guilty, so ruling that she is permitted would be a real new teaching. The next step questions this.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives the answer
Becoming weak or wasting away

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
In a woman who becomes weak.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think a woman who weakened after drinking is guilty.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה teaches that even such a woman is permitted to her husband.

steps.title: If she weakened, didn't the water show she is guilty?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב הונא: weakening after drinking is the water's sign of guilt.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman who becomes weak? The water has already tested her and found her guilty!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב הונא. If she grew weak after drinking, that looks like the water's proof that she sinned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Getting sick after the water usually means the water 'caught' her. So how could the משנה say she is permitted to her husband? רב הונא's case seems to backfire.

keyTerms.meaning: The water has tested her

phrases.english: A woman who becomes weak?
But the water has tested her!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב הונא's case definition.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Weakening is the water's sign of guilt, so she should be forbidden, not permitted.

steps.title: She weakened in other limbs, not in the usual way
steps.stepSummary: The weakness is in other limbs, not the usual סוטה signs. One might think she sinned by force, which forbids a כהן's wife, so the משנה teaches she is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means she weakened in other limbs. You might have said: she really did sin, and the water did not test her in the usual way only because she sinned by force, and for a כהן that still makes her forbidden. So the משנה teaches us that she is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sharpens רב הונא's case. She weakened, but not in the belly and thigh the way a guilty סוטה does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the sign was unusual, one could guess she sinned only under force (אונס). That would not forbid an ordinary woman, but it does forbid a כהן's wife. The משנה rules that this odd weakness means nothing, and she is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: By way of other limbs
You might have said (a mistaken assumption)
By force, against her will
It teaches us (the new point)

steps.whatToRemember: An unusual weakness after drinking is not a sign of guilt, so even a כהן's wife stays permitted.
steps.confusionAlert: The weakness in other limbs is not the normal guilty sign. Only the belly and thigh signs from the פסוק show guilt.

phrases.english: In a woman who weakens by way of other limbs.
phrases.notes: Not the belly and thigh that the פסוק names for a guilty סוטה.

phrases.english: You might have said:
This woman really did commit adultery,
and the fact that the water did not test her
in their usual way
phrases.notes: The letter in square brackets is the corrected wording, making it 'their way', meaning the water's usual way.

phrases.english: is because she was with him by force,
and regarding a כהן she is forbidden,
so it teaches us.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רב הונא by refining his case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The unusual weakness means she sinned by force, which forbids a כהן's wife.
steps.terutzMaskana: The unusual weakness proves nothing, and she is permitted to her כהן husband.

steps.title: Isn't it obvious a סריס's wife drinks?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that the wife of a סריס drinks and asks why this needs saying.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wife of a סריס drinks. Isn't that obvious?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next case in the משנה, the wife of a סריס, and asks why it is needed. Their marriage is allowed, so why should she be different?
steps.deeperAnalysis: This opens a new mini-section with the same pattern of 'obvious, so why say it?'. Nothing about her seems to exclude her from drinking.

keyTerms.meaning: The wife of a eunuch (a man who cannot have children)
She drinks (the bitter water)

phrases.english: The wife of a eunuch drinks.
It is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new clause of the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: She is a validly married woman, so of course she drinks.

steps.title: The פסוק 'besides your husband' might have excluded her
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'מבלעדי אישך', implying the husband was with her. A סריס cannot do that, so one might think his wife does not drink.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: The תורה says 'besides your husband', and this man is not able to do that. So the משנה teaches us that she drinks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the mistake the משנה prevents. The פסוק's words 'מבלעדי אישך' might suggest the process is only for a woman whose husband lives with her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Some man lay with you besides your husband' hints that the husband also lay with her. A סריס cannot, so we might have excluded his wife. The משנה rules that she still drinks.

keyTerms.meaning: Besides your husband (במדבר 5:20)
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
Not capable of this

phrases.english: You might have said:
The Torah said 'besides your husband',
and this man is not capable of that,
phrases.notes: He means the סריס cannot have relations with his wife.

phrases.english: so it teaches us.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא about the סריס's wife.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing a possible mistaken reading of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'מבלעדי אישך' limits סוטה to a woman whose husband can be with her.
steps.terutzMaskana: The wife of a סריס drinks.

steps.title: Isn't it obvious a warning works for all forbidden relatives?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that a husband can warn his wife about any of the עריות, and asks why this needs saying.
steps.simpleTranslation: A husband can warn his wife about any of the forbidden relatives. Isn't that obvious?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the next line of the משנה and asks its usual 'Isn't it obvious?'. The answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Any man who could make her forbidden should count for a warning, so including the עריות seems obvious. The גמרא will explain what new point the משנה is teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden relationships, such as close relatives
They warn (the husband's formal warning, קינוי)

phrases.english: One may warn regarding all the forbidden relatives.
It is obvious!

steps.triggerLanguage: עַל יְדֵי כׇּל עֲרָיוֹת מְקַנִּין. פְּשִׁיטָא!
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new clause of the משנה. The answer comes next.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling 'על ידי כל עריות מקנין'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A warning about any man with whom she would be sinning naturally counts, so the clause looks unnecessary.
